decision.reason: event CE weighting reduced starvation but worsened rigid-grid cases beyond the baseline gate

experiment: Target grammar v3 event-token CE weight training gate

interpretation.what_failed: The same run increases rigid-grid attractor cases beyond the baseline gate, so CE weighting is not sufficient as a standalone v3 scaling recipe.
interpretation.what_passed: Moderate event-token CE weighting transfers into free-running continuation and reduces starvation without legality, max-token, boundary, or F1 regressions.

key_findings: The 32-case runtime gate completed with all legal rollouts, zero dead ends, and zero max-token cases.
Second-window starvation improved strongly: 11 baseline cases to 5 CE-weight cases.
Mean F1@100ms improved from 0.639566 to 0.691899, and median event-count ratio stayed inside the 0.80-1.25 gate.
Rigid-grid cases worsened from 7 to 11, so CE weighting alone fails the primary gate and should not be scaled as-is.
Boundary duplication did not worsen: max boundary-event ratio dropped from 0.200000 to 0.041667.
next_step: Mutate v3 toward timing-diversity or grammar-level anti-rigid continuation while keeping CE weighting as a possible ingredient, not a standalone promotion.
